2. दिश् दिश्, f.
 1. A region, or quarter, or point of the compass, Pañc. ii. d. 64.
 2. pl. The parts of the earth, Sund. 2, 26.
 3. pl. Different directions, Rām. 1, 55, 22; 2, 106, 27; repeated तिशो-दिशस् (The one) hither--(the other) thither, Pañc. 129, 20; also sing. (but with सर्वतस्), Nal. 16, 5.
 4. There are variously reckoned four, eight, or ten quarters of the world, Kathās. 15, 137; Man. 1, 13; MBh. 1, 729.
 5. The number ten, Śrut. 36.
 6. A foreign country, Yājñ. 2, 254.
 7. The name of a river, MBh. 6, 327.
 --Comp.
ऽदिश -दिश् + अ, a substitute for दिश् when latter part of comp. adv.; see यथादिशम्, यथाभीष्टदिशम्.
दिशा दिश् + आ, f. A quarter or point of the compass, MBh. 4, 1716.
दिशोभाग दिशोभाग, i. e. दिश् + अस्-भाग, adj. One who betakes himself to his heels, Pañc. 232, 16.

दिष्टि दिष्टि, i. e. दिश् + ति, f. used only in the instr. दिष्ट्या, implying joy or auspiciousness, Thank heaven ! Sāv. 6, 23.
 --Cf. दिश्.
